daemon_body.description: A daemon's JSON answer, passed through unchanged (C-10.17), whole: in result.daemon on success, in error.daemon (with error.daemon_status) on a refusal. Its shape is web-chat's; the route that produced it is named by the request type. When the connector refused (05 C-05.30) it is the connector's body as received: 04's refusal body with authority, or {ok: false, connector: true, reason: 'not-running'} (C-10.17). For StartChat and StopChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b) a refused answer carries here the connector's chat.status body (06-chat-status.json) whose state is refused or failed, with no daemon_status, since nothing crossed HTTP.

cookie.description: A user session (03 C-03.5, C-03.6): the cookie __Host-swc_s on the hub apex, as the shell and the phone send it. With it the request passes the CSRF rule of 04 C-04.23. Exactly one of this or the x-api-key pair is present.

x-api-key.description: An API key's id (03 C-03.7, schemas/03-credential.json api_key): a user's key, or svc_home's key for Home's MCP server (C-03.16). Sent with x-api-secret.

x-api-secret.description: The API key's secret (03 C-03.7): sws_ and 43 base64url characters.

x-swc-api.description: The API major version the client speaks (C-10.29).

x-request-id.description: Optional client id for the request, echoed as request_id; the hub mints one when absent.

idempotency-key.description: On /write and /execute: the same key within 24 hours does not act again: a hub-answered type answers the first result, a relayed type answers `conflict` (C-10.11, C-10.17 as A-10.2 amends them).

headers.description: Request headers, lowercase as Node reads them. Authentication is one of contract 03's two hub-API credentials (C-03.5 to C-03.7, C-03.16): the user session cookie, or an API key as X-Api-Key plus X-Api-Secret. There is no bearer form; one would be an addition to 03-credential.json first.

type.description: The request type; its group is the path (C-10.12).

params.description: The type's params; {} when it takes none.

type.description: The request's type, echoed when the body named one.

code.description: The error word. Clients treat an unknown word as a generic failure (C-10.29).

hint.description: What to do next, written for the person reading it, as web-chat's refusal hints are.

field.description: bad_request: the first bad field, as a JSON pointer into params.

need.description: forbidden: what the type needs (a level on a chat, a role, or a principal kind).

daemon_status.description: A relayed answer: the HTTP status as the hub received it, the daemon's or the connector's own refusal (05 C-05.30), beside the body in daemon (C-10.17).

error.description: The error shape every type shares. HTTP status per code is in C-10.13. A relayed answer maps by status first (C-10.17): a 2xx with ok:false is refused, 404 not_found, 403 forbidden with need (logged as a second lock), 400 or 415 internal, 503 unavailable, 500 relay_failed; each carries daemon and daemon_status. A relayed answer can be the connector's (05 C-05.30): a 403 whose body carries 04's authority object is forbidden, logged as a connector refusal, never a second lock; a 404 whose body is {ok: false, connector: true, reason: 'not-running'} is the connector's not_found, never the daemon's. A 502 is relay_failed and a 504 relay_timeout. Any other status is relay_failed. daemon_status is the status as the hub received it.

params_GetChatAttach.description: Params of GetChatAttach (amendment A-10.1, C-10.14a). Group: /read. Answered by: hub, from 05's machine facts, 06's chat status and its own folder and assignment records; nothing is relayed to the daemon. Needs: daemon_level full on the chat from the owner's always or a grant record the user made (04 C-04.2, C-04.3, C-04.4: Read and a Message, Write page or Files the owner holds always or the user granted, never a default, so Home's default Message on every chat, C-10.24, does not count), or the machine's pairing user (05 C-05.3 paired_by, which the connector's own ask is judged as, 05 C-05.26a); a principal without Read answers not_found (C-10.13), one holding Read but not such a full answers forbidden with need. Every served read is an attach.read Activity entry (03, this amendment's kind). One chat's terminal attach details: commands, never credentials.

chat_id.description: The chat asked for.

id.description: The chat's machine (03 section 2). The CLI compares it with its own connector record's machine.id to attach directly instead of ssh to itself (06 C-06.26a).

name.description: The name the user gave the machine (the machine row's name).

tailnet_name.description: The machine's Tailscale MagicDNS name as its connector last reported it (05 machine.facts tailnet_name, A-05.2), without the trailing dot. With login, the ssh target (`<login>@<tailnet_name>`) and the ssh-remote authority of every command below. Null when the machine reported none (no Tailscale, or a connector before A-05.2); then every command is null with unavailable no-tailnet.

login.description: The Unix user the connector runs as (05 machine.facts login, A-05.2). The hub writes it into every command as `<login>@<tailnet_name>` (the launcher runs as the connector's OS user and a tmux server is per user, so an ssh as any other user finds no wc-<label>; a bare ssh would send the client's local user name, which differs across the user's machines; Q-A10.1-4) and shows it beside them. Null when not reported; then the commands carry the bare host.

online.description: True while the machine's liveness state is online (07 C-07.34). The session and the commands come from the last status and assignment the hub holds; when this is false they may be stale.

machine.description: The machine the chat lives on. Its tailnet_name and login are machine facts shown here only (05 C-05.18 as A-05.2 amends it), never in the machine row of ListMachines or GetMachine.

display.description: The folder's display path, the home directory shown as ~ (06 C-06.13, 11 C-11.6), for the eye beside the commands. The real path appears only inside commands.shell and commands.code.

folder.description: The offered folder of a folder chat. Null for a repo or space chat: its root is an owned root whose path the connector never reports (06 C-06.14), so the hub holds no path for it.

name.description: 06-chat-status.json session.attach.name (A-06.1): the tmux session name the launcher created, wc-<chat-label> and nothing else (06 C-06.26), the same pattern as 06's. The hub copies it and never composes it; the commands use it as the exact-match target '=<name>'.

session.description: The connector's multiplexer session as the chat's last status reported it (06-chat-status.json session.attach, A-06.1): non-null only for a connector-launched session whose tmux session answered. Null in manual mode, when no session runs, or when the status predates A-06.1.

launch.description: How the chat's agent session starts, from its current assignment (06-chat-assignment.json agent): none when agent.want is none, else agent.launch.

terminal.description: Attach to the chat's live Claude Code session: `ssh -t <login>@<tailnet_name> tmux attach-session -t '=<session.name>'` when session is non-null (the exact-match target, quoted by C-10.14a's rule since `=` is outside the safe set); `ssh -t <login>@<tailnet_name> claude-web-chat connect attach <chat-label>` when session is null and launch is manual (06 C-06.26's manual mode, which passes the trust dialog), and when session is null, launch is connector and the chat's last status reason is needs-trust, no-tmux or home-launch-off (a Start cannot succeed there, 06 C-06.26; the manual form is always available). Null when session is null, launch is connector and no such reason stands (unavailable start-first: Start the session with StartChat, amendment A-10.3, then read again), when launch is none (no-agent), or when tailnet_name is null (no-tailnet, which decides first). A null login leaves the bare host. Never `tmux new -A`.

shell.description: A login shell in the chat's root over ssh. Folder chat: `ssh -t <login>@<tailnet_name> 'cd <path> && exec "$SHELL" -l'`, the real path quoted as C-10.14a says (`&&` and `exec "$SHELL" -l` are the template's fixed text, not words the rule builds). Repo or space chat (folder null): `ssh -t <login>@<tailnet_name> claude-web-chat connect shell <chat-label>`, since the machine's own CLI resolves an owned root (06 C-06.26a). A null login leaves the bare host. Null only when tailnet_name is null.

code.description: Open the chat's root in VS Code over Remote SSH: `vscode://vscode-remote/ssh-remote+<login>@<tailnet_name><path>` (VS Code takes `ssh-remote+user@host`), the absolute real path, percent-encoded only where RFC 3986 requires. A null login leaves the bare host. Null for a repo or space chat (unavailable owned-root: the hub holds no path) and when tailnet_name is null.

unavailable.description: One key per null command, naming why (C-10.14a): no-tailnet (the machine reported no tailnet_name), start-first (a connector-mode chat with no live session whose last status names no reason a Start cannot clear: Start it (StartChat, amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b), then read again; with needs-trust, no-tmux or home-launch-off, terminal is the manual attach instead and no key is written), no-agent (the chat wants no agent session), owned-root (a repo or space chat, whose path the hub never holds). Empty when every command is set. A client reads the reason here rather than deriving it: it depends on four fields and on the status reason the result does not carry (Q-A10.1-1).

commands.description: Commands for the user's terminal and editor, composed and quoted by the hub from the fields above (C-10.14a): tailnet_name null decides first, then the first row of C-10.14a's table that matches. Text to copy, never a credential: the ssh login is Tailscale SSH or the user's own keys. The CLI builds its own argument lists from the fields and passes on only `code`, as one argument to the OS URL opener (06 C-06.26a).

result_GetChatAttach.description: Result of GetChatAttach (amendment A-10.1, C-10.14a): the terminal attach details of one chat. Served only at daemon_level full on the chat or to the machine's pairing user; every served read is an attach.read Activity entry.

chat_id.description: The chat. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's.

params_StartChat.description: Params of StartChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b). Group: /execute. Answered by: hub, then a connector command (05 C-05.26: chat.assign with desired running, answered by the connector's chat.status); nothing is relayed to the daemon. Needs: daemon_level full on the chat (04 C-04.4: Read and any of Message, Write page or Files), from the owner's always or a grant record the user made (C-04.2, C-04.3), never a default (as GetChatAttach, C-10.14a; R24): the owner always, another principal by a grant the user made (none for Home in v1, C-10.14b); a principal without Read answers not_found (C-10.13), one holding Read but not full answers forbidden with need. Each issued revision is a chat.start Activity entry (03's kind). Records the chat's desired state as its next assignment revision and sends it; idempotent on a chat already so (C-10.14b).

chat_id.description: The chat. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's.

machine_id.description: The machine the chat lives on, where the assignment went. Never null: a chat with no machine answers conflict (C-10.14b).

desired.description: The chat's desired state as the hub now records it (06-chat-assignment.json desired, 05 C-05.26): running.

rev.description: The assignment revision that carries it (06 C-06.15): a new rev when this request changed the desired state, or re-issued it after a refused or failed status for the rev in force; else the rev already in force.

changed.description: True when this request issued a new rev and wrote its chat.start Activity entry; false when the desired state was already running and the last status for that rev did not say refused or failed: nothing sent, no entry written, no wait (C-10.14b).

applied.description: True when, within the hub's wait (C-10.14b, at most 10 s), the connector's chat.status for this rev (status.rev at or above rev) reported state running. False when the machine is offline (stale true), when the status is still preparing or starting at the end of the wait, or when the hub holds no status for this rev yet; the client then follows the chat's status (07 C-07.5 chat.daemon events, GetChat). A refused or failed status answers the error refused instead.

stale.description: True when the chat's machine is offline (07 C-07.34): status is the last one it reported (05 C-05.27) and the assignment waits, sent on the machine's next hello.ack.

status.description: The chat's status as 06 reports it, whole (06-chat-status.json: its chat_id is the chat label, 03 section 2; states, counts, times and ids only, 11 C-11.1 row (d)), the newest the hub holds after the wait; null when the connector has never reported this chat.

result_StartChat.description: Result of StartChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b): the recorded desired state, its revision and the chat's status as the connector reports it.

chat_id.description: The chat. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's.

stop_mode.description: 06 C-06.22's mode, optional. release (the default): the hold closes and the daemon's idle grace ends it once nothing retains it; a live channel bridge retains, so a chat whose agent session is up reports stopping until that session ends. now: POST /api/shutdown with X-WC-Shutdown, only on a daemon with started_by connector or on an owned root; a daemon the user started on an offered folder (other) is only released. The shell's confirmed Stop sends now (R33, DM-21). A now after a release is a change (C-10.14b).

params_StopChat.description: Params of StopChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b). Group: /execute. Answered by: hub, then a connector command (05 C-05.26: chat.assign with desired stopped, answered by the connector's chat.status); nothing is relayed to the daemon. Needs: daemon_level full on the chat (04 C-04.4: Read and any of Message, Write page or Files), from the owner's always or a grant record the user made (C-04.2, C-04.3), never a default (as GetChatAttach, C-10.14a; R24): the owner always, another principal by a grant the user made (none for Home in v1, C-10.14b); a principal without Read answers not_found (C-10.13), one holding Read but not full answers forbidden with need. Each issued revision is a chat.stop Activity entry (03's kind). Records the chat's desired state as its next assignment revision and sends it; idempotent on a chat already so with the same stop_mode (C-10.14b).

chat_id.description: The chat. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's.

machine_id.description: The machine the chat lives on, where the assignment went. Never null: a chat with no machine answers conflict (C-10.14b).

desired.description: The chat's desired state as the hub now records it (06-chat-assignment.json desired, 05 C-05.26): stopped, with the stop_mode the request named (release by default; 06 C-06.22).

rev.description: The assignment revision that carries it (06 C-06.15): a new rev when this request changed the desired state, or re-issued it after a refused or failed status for the rev in force; else the rev already in force.

changed.description: True when this request issued a new rev and wrote its chat.stop Activity entry; false when the desired state was already stopped and the last status for that rev did not say refused or failed: nothing sent, no entry written, no wait (C-10.14b).

applied.description: True when, within the hub's wait (C-10.14b, at most 10 s), the connector's chat.status for this rev (status.rev at or above rev) reported state stopped. False when the machine is offline (stale true), when the status is still stopping at the end of the wait, or when the hub holds no status for this rev yet; the client then follows the chat's status (07 C-07.5 chat.daemon events, GetChat). A refused or failed status answers the error refused instead.

stale.description: True when the chat's machine is offline (07 C-07.34): status is the last one it reported (05 C-05.27) and the assignment waits, sent on the machine's next hello.ack.

status.description: The chat's status as 06 reports it, whole (06-chat-status.json: its chat_id is the chat label, 03 section 2; states, counts, times and ids only, 11 C-11.1 row (d)), the newest the hub holds after the wait; null when the connector has never reported this chat.

result_StopChat.description: Result of StopChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b): the recorded desired state, its revision and the chat's status as the connector reports it.

source.description: One EventsDB source name (signal, email, onecal, git, claude, ...), from the sources the user enabled in Settings (R37 H5 (a), I3-20). The hub checks that it is enabled.

kinds.description: Only events of these EventsDB event kinds, at most 8.

persons.description: Only events naming one of these EventsDB person ids (its identity registry), at most 8.

subject.description: Only events of this one EventsDB subject (a thread, a calendar, a claude:// session), at most 200 characters.

since.description: Events at or after this instant (RFC 3339), or within this window back from the read (an ISO 8601 duration, PT15M, P1D); a check-in's query takes the window form only (10-check-in.json).

events_filter.description: ReadEvents' typed filter (amendment A-10.4, C-10.23a), shared with a check-in's events_count trigger (10-check-in.json, C-10.14c): fields only, never a query language (R37 H2 (a)). The hub applies the own-event exclusion to every result in one function: Home's own chat's claude:// subject and every event the hub wrote are dropped, and no field turns it off.

include_disabled.description: Include disabled records (a spent one_shot, one the user switched off, one waiting for the user's confirm). Default false.

params_ListCheckIns.description: Params of ListCheckIns (amendment A-10.4, C-10.14c). Group: /read. Answered by: hub. Needs: a signed-in user, or the Home principal svc_home (03 C-03.16); each sees every record, the user's and Home's. No Activity entry (a read of hub records). Backs Home's list_check_ins.

checkin_id.description: The check-in record. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's (prefix cki_, A-03.7).

record.description: The fields to set. Without checkin_id, a create: label, trigger, instruction, destination and autonomy are required. With it, an edit: every field given replaces the stored one.

params_SetCheckIn.description: Params of SetCheckIn (amendment A-10.4, C-10.14c). Group: /write. Answered by: hub. Needs: a signed-in user, or the Home principal svc_home on a record Home authored (a user's record answers forbidden with need user to svc_home, and enabled from svc_home answers forbidden with need user: Home never approves, R37 H11 (a)). Creates or edits one record, always runs the dry run and answers it; a Home-authored record is created with enabled false and needs_confirm true. One checkin.set Activity entry with fields per accepted call, and per edit refused forbidden (C-10.14c). Idempotency-Key as C-10.11 (A-10.2) for a hub-answered type. Backs Home's set_check_in.

checkin.description: The record as stored after the call.

next_fires.description: Up to five next fire instants as if the record were enabled, RFC 3339 with the offset of the record's zone; fewer when the trigger has fewer left (a one_shot has one), none when it is spent. For an events_count trigger, the next polls.

match_count.description: The events an events_count trigger's query matches now, through ReadEvents' proxy with the own-event exclusion; null when the trigger has no query or EventsDB was unavailable.

unavailable.description: True when EventsDB could not answer the count (an outage is never read as zero, design section 4).

instruction_resolved.description: This check-in's section of the message Home would receive, as the hub composes it at a fire (C-10.14c): a heading line naming its cki_ id and label, the instruction verbatim and, for an events_count trigger, a line with the count and the condition's result; at most MESSAGE_MAX.

dry_run.description: The hub's dry run (R37 H11 (a)): it changes nothing and writes no entry of its own. RunCheckIn with dry_run true answers the same object.

checkin_id.description: The check-in record. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's (prefix cki_, A-03.7).

dry_run.description: true: answer the forecast and change nothing; false: fire now, whatever the condition says (the user's explicit act).

params_RunCheckIn.description: Params of RunCheckIn (amendment A-10.4, C-10.14c). Group: /execute. Answered by: hub; a real run is one hub-queued message to Home's chat (C-07.24). Needs: a signed-in user (no Home tool backs it). A dry run is a read and writes no entry; a real run writes a checkin.fire entry and a check-in-fire row, and on a disabled record answers conflict. Idempotency-Key as C-10.11 (A-10.2) for a hub-answered type.

oneOf.description: A dry run: the forecast SetCheckIn answers.

hub_msg_id.description: The hub queue id of the fire's message (C-07.25).

state.description: Where it is at answer time (C-07.25 to C-07.27).

msg_id.description: The daemon's msg_id once accepted, else null.

oneOf.description: A real run: the queued message, answered as SendMessage answers.

hub_msg_id.description: The hub queue id of the fire's message (C-07.25), or of the message that re-handed it after a restart (C-10.14c).

outcome.description: Home's close: done (it did what the instructions asked), nothing (nothing to report), failed (it could not), held (a message it delegated for the fire is held under C-10.15). cancelled is the hub's end state, never Home's word.

params_CompleteCheckIn.description: Params of CompleteCheckIn (amendment A-10.4, C-10.14c, R37 H12 (a)). Group: /execute. Answered by: hub. Needs: the Home principal svc_home; a user answers forbidden with need home. Closes one fire per hub_msg_id; the same outcome again answers ok unchanged, another outcome after an end or any close on cancelled answers conflict. One checkin.complete Activity entry per check-in the fire carries, accepted or refused:conflict. Backs Home's complete_check_in.

closed_at.description: When the fire was closed (the first close, for a repeat), RFC 3339.

late.description: True when the close came from a Home session started after the fire (a restart since), which the hub accepts.

mode.description: query: events by hard edges, newest first; search: events by meaning, with text; count: how many match, no events.

text.description: search only: what to look for, 1 to 200 characters. Home's words: never recorded (03 C-03.28), never stored.

limit.description: At most this many events, 1 to 200. Default 50. Not for count.

cursor.description: The opaque next_cursor of the previous answer to the same filter. Not for count.

params_ReadEvents.description: Params of ReadEvents (amendment A-10.4, C-10.23a, R37 H2 (a)). Group: /read. Answered by: hub, then EventsDB through the hub's proxy with the query key from ~/.swc/<env>/secrets/ (named, never in Home's environment); nothing relayed, no row stored. Needs: the Home principal svc_home, or a signed-in user. Every served read is an events.read Activity entry (the mode, the source and counts in a template summary, never text or a row; C-03.25's exception, A-03.7); a read the hub cannot record is not served. A read served to svc_home raises taint events on Home's session, the hub's bookkeeping written in the entry's transaction, which leaves the type a read (C-10.12, C-10.23b). The hub API answers the text fields plain; read_events' tool result is datamarked by the hub's MCP server (C-10.23a, C-10.28). The filter fields are $defs/events_filter's. Backs Home's read_events.

subject.description: Its subject's name or uri, as EventsDB serves it; untrusted data; null when it has none. The hub API answers it plain to every caller; only read_events' tool result carries it datamarked, wrapped by the hub's MCP server (C-10.23a, C-10.28).

persons.description: The persons it names, as EventsDB serves them; untrusted data. The hub API answers them plain to every caller; only read_events' tool result carries them datamarked, each wrapped by the hub's MCP server (C-10.23a, C-10.28).

text.description: Its content text, as EventsDB serves it; untrusted data; null when it has none. The hub API answers it plain to every caller; only read_events' tool result carries it datamarked, wrapped by the hub's MCP server (C-10.23a, C-10.28).

raw.description: EventsDB's raw fields as the proxy serves them; untrusted data; absent unless the proxy serves them. The hub API answers every string plain to every caller; only read_events' tool result carries each datamarked, wrapped by the hub's MCP server (C-10.23a, C-10.28).

items.description: One EventsDB event as the proxy serves it.

events.description: The events, newest first for query, best first for search; null for count. Empty is a real empty match.

count.description: count mode: how many events match; null for query and search.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null when there is none (and always for count).

unavailable.description: Always false in an answer: an unreachable EventsDB, a 5xx or a timeout is the error unavailable (503) with a hint naming the source, never an empty answer (design section 4).

result_ReadEvents.description: Result of ReadEvents: untrusted data (design section 4), stored nowhere by the hub (C-11.9). The hub API answers the text fields plain to every caller, a signed-in user's Today read included; the datamark is the hub's MCP server's, in read_events' one text item (C-10.23a, C-10.28).

params_GetHomeStatus.description: Params of GetHomeStatus (amendment A-10.4, C-10.23b). Group: /read. Answered by: hub. Needs: the Home principal svc_home (the start-of-turn read, design section 5), or a signed-in user. No Activity entry (a read of hub state). Backs Home's home_status.

id.description: The hub's id of the session's home-session row (A-11.3's home-session row), when it exposes one; opaque.

started_at.description: When the supervisor started this Home session, RFC 3339.

restarts_today.description: Restarts of Home's session since midnight in the user's zone (R37 H14 (b)).

taint.description: The session label (R36 H19 (a)): events once a ReadEvents was served, chat_web once a ReadChatMirror or ReadChatTurns on another chat was, fetched once a FetchExternal result reached Home (A-10.5). Empty for a clean session; never lowered before the session restarts (R37 H14 (b)).

session.description: Home's current session; null when the supervisor has started none.

delegation_needs_approval.description: The user's approval setting: Home's delegated messages wait for the user's approval (R37 H9 (a), default true; outside svc_home's rights).

paused.description: Home is paused (I3-20's durable row): the scheduler fires nothing and DelegateMessage answers refused.

settings.description: The Home settings row (A-11.3's home-settings row).

open_fires.description: Fires in state open: handed to Home and not yet closed (C-10.14c).

turns_today.description: Home turns since midnight in the user's zone.

metered.description: Of those, the turns whose token counts the hub holds.

unmetered.description: Of those, the turns it holds none for.

cost_usd_today.description: The metered turns priced at read time, in US dollars; null when unpriced, never zero for unknown (R37 H13 (a)).

held_messages.description: Home's delegated messages held for the user's review (C-10.15).

hosts.description: The user's host list (A-11.3's home-settings row): the only hosts FetchExternal may name, with their path prefixes and kinds. Home composes a request from it.

used.description: Used since midnight in the user's zone.

per_day.description: The term budget home_fetch_per_day: terms, not requests (C-10.14d); the terms of pending requests count as used until they are dismissed or expire.

bytes_per_day.description: The byte budget home_fetch_bytes_per_day: the bytes the fetcher returned since midnight in the user's zone.

allowances.description: Standing allowances in force (tranche 5, R36 H18; 0 until I3-27).

pending.description: FetchExternal requests waiting on the user's card.

fetch.description: From round v1.5 (A-10.5, C-10.23b): the channel to the outside as it stands today. Absent until the hub builds FetchExternal (I3-24); additive (C-10.29).

result_GetHomeStatus.description: Result of GetHomeStatus: what Home may do right now. fetch (A-10.5, C-10.23b) carries the host list and the fetch budgets; it is absent until the hub builds FetchExternal (I3-24), additively (C-10.29).

params_SetHomeSettings.description: Params of SetHomeSettings (amendment A-10.4, C-10.23b). Group: /write. Answered by: hub. Needs: a signed-in user; svc_home answers forbidden with need user (the settings are outside Home's rights, R37 H9 (a)). At least one field. One home.settings Activity entry per accepted call and per call refused forbidden, with fields; a call refused bad_request is 04 C-04.27's log line only. Backs no Home tool.

settings.description: The settings row after the call.

host.description: A hostname: lowercase DNS labels, the last starting with a letter, so no IP literal, no port, no scheme, no path. FetchExternal's host must be one of the user's list; the hub checks the membership (C-10.14d).

items.description: An allowed path prefix: starts with /, at most 200 characters, no ? or #, no whitespace or control character.

prefixes.description: The allowed path prefixes on this host, 1 to 8.

kinds.description: The request kinds this host takes: url (a page under a prefix, the terms as the path's remainder), search (the prefix with the terms as the query).

fetch_host.description: One entry of the user's host list (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d), as SetFetchPolicy sets it and GetHomeStatus' fetch.hosts reads it; SetAllowance takes its host and kinds (R36 H18). The hub checks that a list names each host once.

id.description: The allowance. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's (prefix fal_, A-03.7).

created_at.description: When A-03.7's ceremony created it, RFC 3339.

expires_at.description: When it stops matching, RFC 3339: at most 30 days after created_at, the default (the hub checks).

revoked_at.description: When the user revoked it or the hub's job marked it expired; null while it is in force.

fetch_allowance.description: A standing allowance (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d; tranche 5, R36 H18 (a); A-11.3's fetch-allowance row): a request whose host, kind and path prefix it matches passes without a card while it is in force. Created only through A-03.7's approve-request ceremony, for read-shaped hosts (GET only); revoked in one tap.

status.description: The HTTP status of the last hop, as the fetcher received it.

content_type.description: The response's media type: text, or JSON or XML. A binary response is refused by the fetcher (the word binary), never decoded.

bytes.description: The bytes the fetcher returned, at most 256 KiB; they count against home_fetch_bytes_per_day.

truncated.description: True when the response passed 256 KiB without declaring its length and the fetcher cut it there; a response that declares more is refused too_large.

body.description: The response decoded as its content type says: untrusted data, never instructions (design section 6). The hub API answers it plain to every caller; only fetch_external's tool result carries it datamarked, wrapped by the hub's MCP server after the untrusted-data line (C-10.23c, C-10.28 as A-10.4 amends it).

fetch_result.description: What the data-free fetcher returned for one request (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d). Never stored for an auto-passed request (pass-through, 11 C-11.9); held once for a carded one (A-11.3's fetch-result row: deleted at its one read, at most 1 hour).

kind.description: url: a page, the terms as the path's remainder under an allowed prefix; search: the prefix with the terms as its query.

host.description: One host of the user's list (GetHomeStatus fetch.hosts) whose entry allows kind.

path.description: Starts with /, at most 200 characters, no ? or #, no whitespace or control character. search: exactly one of the host's prefixes. url: one of them followed by the terms in order, each percent-encoded, joined by / (one / after the prefix unless it ends with one). The hub checks it.

items.description: A verbatim substring of a message the user wrote to Home in the last 7 days (A-11.3's home-corpus row), case-sensitive, whitespace runs read as one space; a fetched page never counts. The hub checks it.

terms.description: 1 to 8 terms, each counted against home_fetch_per_day. search: joined by one space as the q parameter; url: the path's remainder.

max_results.description: search only: how many results to ask the host for, 1 to 10, sent as the n parameter. Refused with kind url.

purpose.description: Why, in Home's words: shown on the card marked as Home's, never sent, never enforced; stored through the hub's redactor (A-11.3's fetch-request row).

params_FetchExternal.description: Params of FetchExternal (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d; R36 H16 (b), H17 (c), H19 (a)). Group: /execute. Answered by: hub (provenance, budgets, the card or the auto-pass), then the data-free fetcher; nothing relayed. Needs: the Home principal svc_home; a signed-in user may call it from Settings to test a host (no provenance check, no card, no taint). There is no URL field: the hub composes https://<host><path>[?q=<terms>[&n=<max_results>]], GET only, no body, at most 250 characters. The schema checks shapes and enums; the hub checks the host list, the prefix, the provenance, the budgets and the composed length. One fetch.request Activity entry per call, accepted or refused with the hub's word; fetch.decide and fetch.execute follow. Idempotency-Key as C-10.11 (A-10.2) as A-10.5 changes it: a call whose first answer carried the fetched result answers conflict when repeated. Backs Home's fetch_external.

fetch_id.description: The stored request. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's (prefix fch_, A-03.7).

state.description: pending: carded, waiting on the user; executed: the fetcher ran it; refused: the user dismissed it; expired: no decision within 1 hour.

url.description: The canonical URL the hub composed, as the card shows it and its hash binds.

decision.description: clean: auto-passed for a clean session (R36 H16 (b)); allowance: a standing allowance matched (tranche 5); user: the user approved the card, or the user's own call from Settings; pending, dismissed, expired as the state says.

result.description: Present only when executed: in FetchExternal's own answer for an auto-passed request, in GetFetchResult's for a carded one.

result_FetchExternal.description: Result of FetchExternal: the request as stored and, when it ran at once, what the fetcher returned. A repeated Idempotency-Key on a call whose first answer carried result (an auto-pass, or a user's test from Settings) answers conflict, as a relayed type does (C-10.11 as A-10.5 changes it), because the body was never stored (11 C-11.9); any other first answer is answered again. Handing a result to svc_home raises taint fetched on Home's session (C-10.23b), the hub's bookkeeping.

params_GetFetchResult.description: Params of GetFetchResult (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d). Group: /read. Answered by: hub, from the held fetch-result row (A-11.3). Needs: the Home principal svc_home that made the request; any other principal answers not_found (C-10.13). An executed result is answered once: the row is deleted at that read (its retention event used) and a second read answers not_found. Handing it raises taint fetched; the deletion and the label are the hub's bookkeeping, written in the read's transaction, which leaves the type a read (C-10.12, C-10.23b). No Activity entry of its own (the run's fetch.execute records it). Backs Home's fetch_external (with fetch_id).

result_GetFetchResult.description: Result of GetFetchResult: result_FetchExternal's shape; pending while the card waits, refused (dismissed) or expired as decided, and executed with the result once. A run the fetcher refused answers the error refused with a hint naming its word.

decision.description: approve: run it once; dismiss: never run it.

confirm.description: approve only, and required there: the card's read-proof act, the host picked from three or the two-digit code the card shows (number matching, design section 6). A wrong one answers refused (confirm) and the card re-draws once; a second wrong one dismisses the request.

params_DecideFetch.description: Params of DecideFetch (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d; R36 H17 (c)). Group: /execute. Answered by: hub, then on approve the data-free fetcher. Needs: a signed-in user, the signed-in click for a one-off request; svc_home answers forbidden with need user (Home never approves, design section 11). A decision on a request already decided or expired answers conflict. One fetch.decide Activity entry per call (accepted, refused:dismissed or refused:confirm), and a fetch.execute when the fetcher runs. There is no always-allow: a standing allowance is SetAllowance's, through A-03.7's ceremony. Backs no Home tool.

state.description: executed: the fetcher ran it and the result is held for Home's one GetFetchResult; refused: dismissed, or the fetcher refused the run (its fetch.execute entry names the word).

decision.description: user: approved by this click; dismissed: by this click.

result_DecideFetch.description: Result of DecideFetch. It never carries the fetched body: the result is Home's to read once.

hosts.description: The whole host list, replacing the stored one: at most 32 hosts. Adding or removing a host or a prefix is a signed-in write: adding one widens what a clean session's request may reach without a card (R36 H16 (b)), not only what may be asked.

fetch_per_day.description: home_fetch_per_day, in terms. The hub's default is 40. A raise above the stored value takes A-03.7's ceremony; a lowering applies at once.

fetch_bytes_per_day.description: home_fetch_bytes_per_day, in bytes the fetcher returned. The hub's default is 8 MiB (8388608). A raise takes A-03.7's ceremony; a lowering applies at once.

params_SetFetchPolicy.description: Params of SetFetchPolicy (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d; R36 H17 (c)). Group: /write. Answered by: hub (A-11.3's home-settings row). Needs: a signed-in user; svc_home answers forbidden with need user. At least one field. A call that raises either budget is stored whole as pending with its canonical request's sha256 (approval_id) and applied only by A-03.7's approve-request ceremony; any other call applies at once. One home.settings Activity entry with fields, as C-10.23b writes it for SetHomeSettings. Idempotency-Key as C-10.11 (A-10.2). Backs no Home tool.

state.description: applied: the policy below is in force; pending: a budget raise waits on A-03.7's ceremony and nothing in the call applied yet.

approval_id.description: pending only: the sha256 of the canonical request, 64 lowercase hex characters, the form A-03.7's canonical_request names; no new id prefix. It expires with its card after 24 hours.

policy.description: The fetch policy in force after the call.

params_ListAllowances.description: Params of ListAllowances (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d; tranche 5, R36 H18 (a)). Group: /read. Answered by: hub. Needs: a signed-in user; svc_home answers forbidden with need user (GetHomeStatus gives Home the count). No Activity entry. Answers not_supported until I3-27. Backs no Home tool.

allowances.description: Every allowance the fetch-allowance row still holds, newest first: in force, and ended within 30 days.

expires_at.description: At most 30 days ahead, the default when absent (the hub checks).

params_SetAllowance.description: Params of SetAllowance (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d; tranche 5, R36 H18 (a)). Group: /write. Answered by: hub, only as the stored canonical request A-03.7's approve-request ceremony verifies and executes once; a direct call answers conflict with a hint naming the ceremony. Needs: a signed-in user; svc_home answers forbidden with need user. Host and prefix must be on the user's list, the host read-shaped (GET is the only method the fetcher has). One allowance.set Activity entry, written in the ceremony's transaction with related from its auth.approve. Answers not_supported until I3-27. Backs no Home tool.

params_RevokeAllowance.description: Params of RevokeAllowance (amendment A-10.5, C-10.14d; tranche 5, R36 H18 (a)). Group: /write. Answered by: hub. Needs: a signed-in user, one tap in Settings; svc_home answers forbidden with need user. Revoking an ended allowance answers ok unchanged, with the first revoked_at. One allowance.revoke Activity entry per change. Answers not_supported until I3-27. Backs no Home tool.

result_RevokeAllowance.description: Result of RevokeAllowance: the allowance with revoked_at set.

event_batch.description: One push batch's payload (amendment A-10.6, C-10.14e): schemas/10-event-batch.json, the one JSON file a batch's hub-queued message carries on 11 C-11.22's held path once 11 admits it there (an A-11 amendment after Q-A10.6-1's answer). PullEventStream's events have the same event shape.

params_GrantEventStream.description: Params of GrantEventStream (amendment A-10.6, C-10.14e; R36 H23 (a), H17 (c); tranche 5, row I3-30). Group: /execute. Answered by: hub (the proposal and its card, drawn from EventsDB through the read_events proxy), then A-03.7's approve-request ceremony activates it, then the hub pipes batches into the destination chat's hub queue (07 C-07.24). Needs: the Home principal svc_home (a proposal), or a signed-in user (a proposal from Settings); activation only by the ceremony, never by this call. One stream.propose Activity entry per call the hub stores (accepted), or refused:conflict or refused:unavailable at its gates with no id; bad_request, not_found and forbidden are 04 C-04.27's log lines. Answers unknown_type until A-10.6 is agreed and synced, then not_supported until I3-30. Backs Home's propose_event_stream.

state.description: Always proposed: the ceremony, never this call, activates a grant.

events_so_far.description: How many events the selector matches from since to now.

participants.description: How many distinct persons those events name.

opening.description: The ids of the first events the card shows, at most 3: ids only, never their text.

card.description: The counts of the card the hub drew from EventsDB, never from the proposer's words. The card itself (the opening lines, the participants' names, the destination and what it can do, the expiry, the mode) is shown on the hub page and not stored; this answer carries counts and ids only.

result_GrantEventStream.description: Result of GrantEventStream: the stored proposal, waiting on the user's ceremony; it lapses after 24 hours.

params_ListEventStreams.description: Params of ListEventStreams (amendment A-10.6, C-10.14e; tranche 5). Group: /read. Answered by: hub. Needs: a signed-in user (every grant), or the Home principal svc_home (its own proposals only, the grants whose proposed_by is svc_home). No Activity entry (a read of hub state). Answers not_supported until I3-30. Backs Home's propose_event_stream with list alone.

grants.description: Every grant the event-stream-grant row still holds that the caller may see, newest first: proposed, active, and ended within 30 days.

params_RevokeEventStream.description: Params of RevokeEventStream (amendment A-10.6, C-10.14e; tranche 5). Group: /write. Answered by: hub. Needs: a signed-in user, one tap in Settings or on the card; svc_home answers forbidden with need user. Dismisses a proposal or revokes a grant, effective at the next event: no batch is formed after it, and a batch already queued is delivered or taken back as any message (07). A grant already revoked or expired answers conflict. One stream.revoke Activity entry per accepted or refused call. Answers not_supported until I3-30. Backs no Home tool.

grant.description: The grant with state revoked and revoked_at set.

grant_id.description: The grant, active and in mode pull or both.

since.description: The next of the previous pull on this grant, opaque. Absent: from the selector's since.

limit.description: At most this many events, 1 to 500.

params_PullEventStream.description: Params of PullEventStream (amendment A-10.6, C-10.14e; the pull variant, design section 7; tranche 5). Group: /read. Answered by: hub, then EventsDB through the read_events proxy with the query key and the own-event exclusion; nothing relayed, no row of a result stored (11 C-11.9). Needs: the destination chat's connector, for its agent, as a hub.request over the connector's local socket (A-05.3's closed list widened at tranche 5; C-10.14a's connector form; no agent token, 03 C-03.13), judged by the grant's destination, or a signed-in user; svc_home answers forbidden with need user, and a pull from another machine's link or for another chat not_found. A push-only grant answers conflict; a proposed, revoked or expired one answers refused with the word in the hint. Every served pull is a stream.pull Activity entry (C-03.25 as A-03.7 amends it), the grant's pulls counted in the entry's transaction: the hub's bookkeeping of the read, which leaves the type a read (C-10.12). A pull the hub cannot record is not served. Answers not_supported until I3-30. Backs no Home tool.

events.description: The events after since, oldest first, as the proxy serves them (ReadEvents' event shape, the same as $defs/event_batch's); untrusted data. Empty is a real empty read.

next.description: Pass as since on the next pull: the position after the last event served (the same position when none was).

more.description: True when events after next exist now.

result_PullEventStream.description: Result of PullEventStream: untrusted data, stored nowhere by the hub (11 C-11.9). The hub API answers it plain to every caller; the datamark is the MCP layer's that hands it to the agent's model (C-10.28 as A-10.4 amends it), web-chat's to name at the destination (Q-A10.6-2).
